title: Coral and the Garden Revisited
premise: Sable Sandoval has spent his life in the valley of Vell, where a broken covenant keeps magic out and thieves like him safe from the sorcerous Order that rules beyond the ridgeline. When he steals a memory that turns out to be his own face in a century-old prophecy, he learns the covenant is failing and the long winter falling on both realms will end everything unless it is reforged. Hunted by the Order's memory-eaters and betrayed by the lover who wrote him into prophecy, Sable must choose between the belonging he built in Vell and the truth that he was born to be its sacrifice. In the end, he reforges the covenant not with his death but by surrendering every stolen memory—including his own name—becoming the valley's living anchor, remembered by no one but needed by all.
about_author: August Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing letters in a flooded coastal town before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about small places, stubborn people, and the bargains we make to stay ourselves.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Kept Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He lifts a memory from a dying ferryman—his last job before winter closes the passes—and finds among the stolen images a vision of himself standing in a garden that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: A Book Older Than the Valley
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with interludes from archivist Wren Odile. In the flooded archive beneath Vell's chapel, Sable finds the Prophecy of the Garden Revisited, written a century ago, naming 'the thief with tonight's date' as covenant-keeper. Beat: vertigo—the discovery that his anonymity was always a story someone else wrote.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Chance
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Sable's lover Ilsa reveals she sought him out deliberately: her family were the prophecy's original scribes, and she chose him because the text demanded it. Beat: betrayal braided with tenderness; loyalty and truth begin their war for Sable's heart.

chapters.title: What the Winter Eats
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The long winter arrives early—frost that erases memories instead of warmth. The Order's memory-eaters cross the ridge where magic should fail, proving the covenant is already broken. Beat: dread; the valley's safety revealed as an illusion already lost.

chapters.title: The Order of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured by the Order, Wren learns they want Sable alive: the covenant can only be reforged at its breaking point, and the prophecy's thief must consent. Beat: moral complication—the enemy claims to be saving the world too.

chapters.title: Garden Revisited
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following the ferryman's stolen memory, Sable reaches the ruined garden where the covenant was first sworn and meets the ghost of its last keeper, who shows him the price: a soul surrendered whole. Beat: temptation and terror; power offered as salvation.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa betrays Sable's location to the Order to save her family, then reverses herself when she sees what the Order truly intends—to bind Sable permanently as their instrument. Beat: guilt-driven reversal; she chooses truth over blood, too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the garden's heart, Sable faces the Order's High Keeper and refuses both their binding and the ghost's simple sacrifice, proposing a third way: the covenant anchored in a living, willing mind. Beat: defiance; climax begins as the winter presses to its darkest hour.

chapters.title: Every Memory He Ever Stole
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, dissolving into fragments. To reforge the covenant, Sable pours every stolen memory back into the world and offers his own—name, past, self—as the anchor. Ilsa holds him through the unmaking. Beat: sacrificial climax; identity surrendered willingly rather than taken.

chapters.title: The Man With No Yesterday
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, one year later. Spring returns; the valley thrives under a quiet guardian no one remembers, a gentle stranger who tends the garden. Ilsa visits daily, keeping his story alive even though he cannot hold it. Beat: bittersweet resolution—belonging achieved at the cost of being known, love persisting without recognition.
